question: Walk me through this TCP three-way handshake: what do the SYN, Seq and Ack values in each of the three segments mean, and why is the first acknowledgement number 1024?
reference_answer: 1) Client A -> server B: SYN=1, Seq=1023 (A's initial sequence number), ACK flag 0 (nothing to acknowledge yet). 2) B -> A: SYN-ACK: SYN=1, ACK=1, Seq=2131691 (B's own initial sequence number), Ack number 1024 = 1023 + 1 - the SYN consumes one sequence number, so 1024 is the next byte B expects from A. 3) A -> B: ACK=1, SYN=0, Seq=1024, Ack number 2131692 = 2131691 + 1 (acknowledges B's SYN). Both sides now know each other's sequence numbers: the connection is established and data can flow (the third segment can already carry data).

checks.name: client_syn_1023
checks.description: Segment 1: the client's SYN carries its initial sequence number 1023.

checks.name: server_isn_2131691
checks.description: Segment 2 (SYN-ACK): the server picks its own initial sequence number 2131691.

checks.name: ack_1024_is_1023_plus_1
checks.description: Ack number 1024 = 1023 + 1: the SYN uses one sequence number, 1024 is the next byte expected.

checks.name: final_ack_2131692
checks.description: Segment 3: the client acknowledges with Ack number 2131692 = 2131691 + 1.

checks.name: third_seq_1024_established
checks.description: Segment 3 has Seq 1024 and completes the handshake (connection established, data can flow).
